text: For quadrilaterals within circles, the (sum of the) opposite angles is equal to two right-angles. Let $ABCD$ be a circle, and let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral within it. I say that the (sum of the) opposite angles is equal to two right-angles.
Therefore, since the three angles of any triangle are equal to two right-angles [Prop.~1.32], the three angles $CAB$, $ABC$, and $BCA$ of triangle $ABC$ are thus equal to two right-angles.
assertion: the three angles CAB, ABC, and BCA of triangle ABC are equal to two right-angles

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the three angles of any triangle are equal to two right-angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: three angles $CAB$, $ABC$, and $BCA$ of triangle $ABC$ are thus equal to two right-angles

text: And $CAB$ (is) equal to $BDC$. For they are in the same segment $BADC$ [Prop.~3.21].

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: they are in the same segment $BADC$

text: And $ACB$ (is equal) to $ADB$. For they are in the same segment $ADCB$ [Prop.~3.21].

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: they are in the same segment $ADCB$

text: Thus, the whole of $ADC$ is equal to $BAC$ and $ACB$.
assertion: the whole angle ADC equals BAC plus ACB

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the whole of $ADC$ is equal to $BAC$ and $ACB$

text: Thus, $ABC$, $BAC$, and $ACB$ are equal to $ABC$ and $ADC$.
assertion: angles ABC, BAC, ACB together equal angles ABC and ADC

text: But, $ABC$, $BAC$, and $ACB$ are equal to two right-angles. Thus, $ABC$ and $ADC$ are also equal to two right-angles.
assertion: angles ABC and ADC are equal to two right-angles

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: $ABC$, $BAC$, and $ACB$ are equal to two right-angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $ABC$ and $ADC$ are also equal to two right-angles

text: Similarly, we can show that angles $BAD$ and $DCB$ are also equal to two right-angles.
assertion: angles BAD and DCB are also equal to two right-angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: angles $BAD$ and $DCB$ are also equal to two right-angles

text: Thus, for quadrilaterals within circles, the (sum of the) opposite angles is equal to two right-angles. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
